state: An unimplemented typed business-language draft needs a private AI-assisted workbench for a named company task. Its first tools are existing task-owner mutations: generated Task.update under membership plus current employee/workplace guards, and an exported complete(task) under the same current guards and not-done condition. Generated input metadata already belongs to those operations. Existing action values name a finite operation set and freeze record identities/versions, but leave other arguments as later form inputs; they cannot be cast from model text or JSON. Typed asynchronous capabilities, retained delivery outcomes, records, locks, current viewer reads and same-principal canonical calls already exist. A provider documents tools as model-produced names/arguments which the host dispatches, and schema-constrained output still needs host validation. The workbench must freeze bounded authorized task context, obtain at most one suggested change per model step, show the exact operation and complete normalized arguments, require its real worker to approve, recheck context and record versions plus present owner authority, and retain the attempt on failure. Cancellation, reconnect, finite step/output limits and untrusted-text containment must work. Model data cannot choose arbitrary code, a new tool, another principal or records outside the request context. No compiler/runtime implementation constrains draft redesign. Compare the same business outcome and total authored/shared mechanism, with no measured token or runtime result.

representation.instructions: Which representation best supports this bounded approval and canonical execution journey?

criteria.explicit: Keep existing language only: define a closed app-owned proposal contract for each permitted operation, explicitly copy its relevant argument fields and context versions, and branch to its static owner call after approval. Existing checks and typed values remain sufficient; adding/changing tools requires corresponding schema and dispatch edits, with drift risk and plainly visible local logic.
criteria.invocation: Add one finite full-invocation value type derived from owner operations, containing the complete normalized arguments and frozen record versions. Permit typed provider proposals only against the request's frozen authorized reference set, and call an approved value through ordinary same-principal admission. App still owns step limits, context refresh, approval and business state. This reduces repeated DTO/dispatch code while requiring precise new value validation, preview, provenance and invocation semantics.
criteria.toolset: Declare a named finite toolset from canonical reads/mutations, with a generated planning interface and typed proposed-call output. The shared mechanism derives schemas, validates request-bound references and persists proposal/approval correlation; app configures bounded steps and current-authority approval policy. This can consolidate more orchestration and repeated schemas, but introduces a broader declaration and lifecycle contract whose failure and context rules must stay explicit.
